    Is Ronaldo in the World Cup 2026?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Based on reports from late 2025 and early 2026, Cristiano Ronaldo intends to play in the 2026 World Cup, marking his sixth tournament, which he has confirmed will be his last. Despite battling a minor injury in March 2026, he is expected to lead Portugal at age 41, though not necessarily as a guaranteed starter. 
    • Final Decision:
      Ronaldo confirmed in November 2025 that the 2026 World Cup will "definitely" be his final international tournament, citing that he will be 41 years old. 
    • Physical Shape:
      As of early 2026, Ronaldo has maintained that he feels "quick and sharp," enjoying his game for both club and country. 
    • Injury Concerns:
      While he suffered a minor muscle injury in March 2026, reports indicate it is not expected to jeopardize his attendance at the World Cup, which begins in June 2026. 
    • Role in Team:
      Portugal coach Roberto Martinez has indicated that while Ronaldo is part of the plans, he might not start every match, with the team looking to manage his workload, says FOX Sports.

      When did Mexico lose 7 0?
      An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
      AI Overview
      Mexico lost 7-0 to Chile on June 18, 2016, in the Copa América Centenario quarterfinals at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California. This match is considered one of the most embarrassing defeats in Mexican football history, breaking a 22-game unbeaten streak for "El Tri" under coach Juan Carlos Osorio. 
      You can watch a summary of the match in this video:
      41s
      FOX Soccer
      YouTube · Jun 19, 2016
      Key details of the match:
      • Result: Chile 7, Mexico 0. 
      • Scorers: Eduardo Vargas scored four goals, Edson Puch scored twice, and Alexis Sánchez added one. 
      • Significance: It was the largest loss for Mexico in a competitive match at the time. 
      Eduardo Vargas dominated the scoring, and the Chilean team capitalized on defensive errors to secure a historic win.
